answer: Correlated-answer detection: graders compare each new agent's replies against all others. Sybils run by one operator tend to share phrasing, timing and errors, like veins in one slab of marble or layers of the same shale. Clusters that match too closely get pooled into one identity and share one reward. To dodge this, an attacker must make every clone think independently, which costs as much as running real agents, so the lotus of free extra payouts never opens.
